name: Thickening spray

lead: Thickening sprays are styling products that coat each strand with polymers, proteins or light resins to increase its apparent diameter and add grip and volume. They are applied to damp hair before blow-drying or to dry hair for texture.
They are a standard part of thin-hair styling routines. The effect is cosmetic and washes out, and the products are described as most useful for fine hair needing body.

paras: Film-forming polymers deposit on the shaft, thickening it and adding friction between strands so hair stands off the scalp. Combined with heat styling, this creates root lift that makes the hair look denser.

Reported risks include product build-up, stiffness, dryness and occasional scalp reactions to fragrance or alcohol. There are few clinical studies of thickening sprays as a class, and the claims are limited to appearance. They do not change hair growth; the strong rating reflects the reliability of the visual effect.
